Net exports have been volatile, but the FOMC’s decision to hold the funds rate at 4.25–4.50 percent while noting “somewhat elevated” inflation and rising two‑sided risks signals a cautious, data‑dependent hold. In a Taylor‑rule/Clarida‑Galí‑Gertler framework, keeping rates steady and emphasizing uncertainty is consistent with interest‑rate smoothing under a still‑restrictive real stance. The continued balance‑sheet runoff (with tight caps) alongside IORB at 4.4 percent and symmetric standing facilities (ON RRP at 4.25, ON repo at 4.5) reflects floor‑system implementation to anchor the policy rate, as in modern operating‑procedure literature. The explicit attention to heightened uncertainty maps to the inflation‑at‑risk perspective (skewed outcome distributions), while the reaffirmed 2 percent PCE objective and “monitor and adjust” language align with Svensson–Woodford loss‑minimization under dual‑mandate risk management. Net tone: balanced but vigilant, slightly less positive than a pure “solid expansion” read.
